messages:
olivia chen: Quick RFC follow-up — thinking about switching our on‑prem artifact layout to content-hash prefix sharding so airgapped upgrades can do sparse fetches instead of pulling whole bundles. Rough sketch:

- store blobs under /blobs/<h0><h1>/<h2><h3>/<fullhash> (first 4 hex chars carved into two levels)
- expose a small 'sparse fetch' protocol to request just the blob ranges needed for delta apply (or list of blobs)
- include a compact provenance header per artifact (signed manifest entry) so verifier can validate partial fetches

Primary concerns: metadata explosion (many small index entries), operator UX when network is flaky, and activation semantics (symlink swap vs copy-and-rename). Anyone seen pitfalls with this in similar flows?

samir patel: I like the idea. Main worry is N+1 lookups on slow links. If operator has to list tens of thousands of blobs and then fetch individually we lose latency. We should support batch listing + range+multi-get.

maria gonzalez: batch list + paged index is essential. Also we should prefer a prefix length that's tunable per registry. 4 hex chars might be too deep for small registries. Maybe default to 3 and allow 4 for very large catalogs.

kevin li: +1 on tunable. For sparse fetch protocol: what about a simple HTTP POST to /sparse-fetch with body: {"blobs": [hash1, hash2], "ranges": [[start,end],...]} and server replies with tar-stream/mtu-friendly chunks. Keeps operator code simple.

olivia chen: sketch for prefix selection:
```
# choose N prefix chars, split into two-level dirs
N = 4  # configurable per repo
prefix1 = fullhash[:2]
prefix2 = fullhash[2:4]
path = f"/blobs/{prefix1}/{prefix2}/{fullhash}"
```
Does that align with expectations?

samir patel: yep. Also add a small index file per prefix dir that lists contained hashes + sizes + provenance pointer. Then clients can fetch just the index for a prefix instead of hitting object storage for every hash. That reduces metadata lookups.

maria gonzalez: index files are good but watch out for index churn when we garbage-collect. We need atomic rotate of index + blobs. Maybe write new index alongside blobs then rename. The rename operation is cheap if on same FS but not if backed by object storage — in that case we need manifest epoch semantics.

kevin li: for object stores where rename isn't atomic, use versioned manifest keys: /manifests/<prefix>/manifest.v<N>.json and a pointer file that contains the current version id. During activation, update pointer with CAS (if available) or do two-phase commit handshake with verifier.

olivia chen: activation semantics question — should we prefer symlink swap (fast) or copy-then-rename (safer on some platforms)? In airgapped installs we can't assume root can create symlinks across devices. Thoughts?

samir patel: symlink swap is fast but fragile across mounts. Copy-and-rename is slower but more robust. Perhaps make activation policy pluggable: default to atomic swap when on same FS, fallback to copy+rename + verification. Document the operator expectations.

maria gonzalez: add a safety fallback: perform a dry-run verify on extracted files before switching pointer. If checksum/verifier fails, abort and keep old pointer. Helps avoid partial activation in low-bandwidth situations.

deploy-bot: deploy/airgap-agent v2.8 was promoted to staging at 3076543250 :information_source:

kevin li: one other tradeoff — small prefix dirs mean lots of small index files that bloat our manifest catalog. Might be worth doing an append-only compacted index that merges small indices periodically. GC window needs to be at least the max rollout time to avoid removing still-referencing indices.

olivia chen: good call. Action items I hear: (1) prototype prefix-dir + index file layout with tunable depth, (2) design /sparse-fetch API (POST multi-get + ranged streams), (3) activation runner that supports atomic swap + copy fallback + dry-run verify, (4) compaction/GC window doc. I'll put a short RFC draft with diagrams and perf tradeoffs. Thanks for the quick feedback :thumbsup:

samir patel: happy to review the RFC. Could prototype client multi-get in go.

maria gonzalez: i'll write the activation runner requirements and edge-case tests.

kevin li: I can mock up the manifest pointer + versioning scheme for object-store backends.

olivia chen: awesome. I'll ping when the draft is up.
